old: title: "Fresh re-marking two-port quotient. Rooted two-port states [C; s, t] evolve by fresh (unnamed, multiset) re-marking along Hamilton paths from s to t followed by complement. (a) The free classes of two-sided gluings k*h*k' with rooted contexts of order <= 2 already separate all strong joint two-port classes, so no closed compression of the joint class exists for strong states. (b) One-sided gluings never separate the one-sided collision pairs, but closure under the dynamics separates all of them. (c) The port-forgotten line-response histogram of a strong atom determines the atom. (d) If only the unrooted class must be determined at every step, the fresh-re-marking quotient is a proper compression. This is the stochastic quotient left open by the vitali-response packet's C5."
new: title: "Fresh re-marking two-port quotient. Rooted two-port states [C; s, t] evolve by fresh (unnamed, multiset-counted) re-marking along Hamilton paths from s to t followed by complement (V1), or along all Hamilton paths with ports reset (V2). (a) PROVED (audit reconstruction lemma): already the single sandwich e*h*e determines every strong joint two-port class for n >= 3, so the static observer of the two-sided gluings k*h*k' with contexts of order <= 2 trivially admits no closed compression on strong states (scalar two-sided observers such as H(e*h*e) do compress). (b) One-sided gluings depend only on the one-sided classes (PROVED) and never separate the one-sided collision pairs; one V1 step, whose successor multiset is a joint-port statistic, separates all of them even from the bare class observation (FINITE-EXACT n <= 7); V2 separates none. (c) The port-forgotten line-response histogram of a strong atom determines the atom (FINITE-EXACT n <= 7; even the set of partner classes does). (d) If only the unrooted class must be determined at every step, the V1 quotient is a proper compression (FINITE-EXACT n = 4..7); the V2 quotient is the class partition (PROVED, trivial). This is an analogue, on two-port classes and with counted multisets, of the stochastic quotient mentioned in vitali-response C5, not that quotient."
why: Statements (a) and part of (b), (d) are one-line theorems (audit); (b) is a joint-port effect of V1 by construction, not an upgrade of one-sided data; the identification with the C5 quotient is inexact (different carrier X_n vs two-port classes, counts vs distributions: the normalized-distribution quotient is coarser, 11031 vs 11033 strong cells for free at n = 7).

old: 1. **Joint classes are minimal (two-sided).** For every `n ≥ 5`, the static observation `glue2` separates any two distinct strong joint two-port classes. So no closed compression of the joint class exists for strong states, even without the dynamics.
new: 1. **Joint classes are minimal for the two-sided gluing observer: PROVED, trivially.** For every `n ≥ 3` the single two-sided gluing `e*h*e` determines a strong two-port state. In `e*h*e` the added entrance vertex `a` has out-degree 1 and the added exit vertex `b` has in-degree 1. Since `C` is strong, the only other vertex of out-degree 1 can be `s` (when `d⁺_C(s) = 1`), whose out-neighbour has out-degree at least 2, and the only other vertex of in-degree 1 can be `t`, whose in-neighbour has in-degree at least 2. As `a → s` and `t → b`, the vertices `a` and `b` are determined, and `s = N⁺(a)`, `t = N⁻(b)`, `C = e*h*e − {a, b}` (audit `sandwich_reconstruction.py`). Hence `glue2` separates any two distinct strong joint two-port classes in every order (through `n = 7` each of its nine contexts does so alone), and no closed compression refining it exists. This concerns this observer only: the two-sided scalar observer `sand = H(e*h*e)` does compress (5889 strong V1 cells of 14162 at `n = 7`).
why: The former statement ("for every n >= 5", OPEN) is a one-line theorem valid from n = 3; the computational fact adds nothing beyond it.
